Quand on croit aux jeunes – le pari du s: When We Believe in Young People: The Bet Behind Studio NBS
« Je parle le langage qu’ils parlent. So: “I speak the language they speak. Often, people just need to be heard”
Le studio de musique NBS est situé dans: The NBS music studio is located in a youth centre in Côte-des-Neiges. It gives the neighbourhood's up-and-coming talent the chance to record and produce songs for free. More than just a space where young people can make music, it is a sanctuary where they are heard and can thrive, sheltered from society's judgment and rejection. Between recording sessions, La Converse went to meet these determined artists.
Une dizaine de jeunes sont présents au s: About a dozen young people are at the studio. They sit relaxed while one of their own, Ghost, raps his new track in the recording booth. Little by little, they tell us about their relationship with the studio and reveal what brought them to this space. One thing their paths have in common? Most of them don't feel valued in the outside world.
Entre les murs du studio, ils trouvent u: Within the studio's walls, they find a different atmosphere. The neighbourhood's young people talk about their daily lives and the issues that weigh on them. One of them is mixing. That's when you realize the studio's goal isn't only to let young people rap. The program trains them so that one day they can perform on stage, record and mix. “We're also a program made by youth for youth; we hire young people who have come through the studio so that they become mentors to other young people,” explains the studio's director, Jai Nitai, who is also a rapper and music producer. For many at the studio, Jai is more than a director: he is a confidant and a mentor. “Young people went through a lot during the pandemic,” says the studio director. “They have to deal with things on the street, at home, at school. I'm not going to judge them for the bad choices they've made; I'm going to see them as people who are capable of getting better. So they come to me with all kinds of situations, some more extreme than others. I can't reveal anything, but I tell them I'm here for them, and I use every resource at my disposal to help them meet people who can help with the particular problems they have.”
Avec son bagage en hip-hop, l’artiste et: With his background in hip-hop, the artist and youth worker manages to get to the heart of the issues the neighbourhood's young people face. “I speak the language they speak. Often, people just need to be heard,” says Jai Nitai.
« Beaucoup de jeunes viennent au studio,: “A lot of young people come to the studio, kids who do bad things outside,” confides Ghost, a rapper and studio regular. “They come here and, with the energy of the studio, they can't escape their reality, but the time they spend here saves them from the bad things they could be doing outside.”
Le discours de Ghost fait écho à celui d: Ghost's words echo those of all the other young people. They all agree on two things. The first is that young people in Côte-des-Neiges have to deal with many problems in their daily lives. The second is that the studio helps them face those problems. “Young people in Côte-des-Neiges have been through a lot of hardship,” explains TP, a rapper and sound engineering student. Their statements take on their full meaning when you consider Côte-des-Neiges's socio-economic context. There are many disparities in the neighbourhood. <l1>Access to employment and affordable housing is a major difficulty for its mostly immigrant population.</l1>
Les jeunes du quartier ont aussi dû fair: The neighbourhood's young people have also had to cope with the tragic loss of one of their own. Last October, a young man named Janai was <l1>stabbed in Côte-des-Neiges and died of his injuries a few hours later</l1>. That is only the visible side of the issues they face. Because, in a more insidious harm, loneliness sometimes affects some of them. To try to ease these problems, NBS studio steps in as a new family for them. “NBS is like a community,” TP tells us. “What we do here… We come and we give back to the Côte-des-Neiges community. It's not just free. We're given a ‘paradise,’ a place where we, the youth, can express ourselves. [...] For me, NBS is a special place, a very special place,” he says, as his peers nod in agreement.
De la ville de Châteauguay au sous-sol d: From the city of Châteauguay to the basement of the Chalet Kent in Côte-des-Neiges, it's a good distance to travel to get to a studio. Yet that is the journey young artist Iqua makes. She started singing at the age of five, and today she uses her art as therapy. The young rapper, who is a psychology student, uses her songs as a way to express herself. “A song I want to record is more about mental health, because I have social anxiety. I don't know how I'm managing to talk to you right now,” she exclaims, laughing. “It's really that. It's really stuff about me. It's really matters of the heart,” says Iqua.
« Quand j’étais plus jeune, la manière d: “When I was younger, the way I saw this life made me unhappy, especially living in Uptown, because Uptown is not a good place to live.” The statement from Yama, a sound engineer at NBS studio, lands like a blow. He sits in his chair with a bass in his hands. Behind him, a computer is on; several sound-mixing applications are open on the screen. He shares his life with us while playing his instrument and working on tracks. As his story unfolds, it becomes clear that he perfectly embodies the spirit of the studio. Having grown up in Côte-des-Neiges, the young sound engineer had a difficult childhood.
Yama, ingénieur du son et producteur au: Yama, sound engineer and producer at NBS studio. Photo: Ramy Berkani
Pour Yama , le plus important c’est de p: For Yama, the most important thing is to share his knowledge with young people who, like him, are passionate about music. Having grown up in Uptown – the name young people give to a part of Côte-des-Neiges – Yama says he never felt understood by society, and more specifically by school. Many of the young people in the room confirm that they have felt the same way.
« Quand tu vas à l’extérieur ou dans une: “When you go outside or into a social structure like school, where the teacher is part of the school system and has received an education, an education your family doesn't have, how can you communicate with someone who doesn't understand you?” he asks. “That's why some people don't take school seriously. Because they don't identify with their teachers.” Misunderstood at school and fleeing problems at home, he himself ended up at NBS studio. “I just needed a place to escape to, and NBS was around the corner,” the young man explains. “I skipped class because I didn't want to go home or go to school. I would just go to NBS. It's really a place you come to when you're feeling down, and without knowing why, once you're here, you feel better.” Yama's relationship with music began before he arrived at the studio 10 years ago. When he was younger, the artist took music classes at his school. And like all young people, he also dreamed of a career as a great rapper. “But rapping wasn't for me,” he says with a smile. “So I stopped and focused on beatmaking instead.”
Yama a fréquenté le studio pendant plus: Yama has been coming to the studio for more than 10 years. He now works there and is committed to giving young people the kind of support he received. He is also proud of having set up NBS's structure with Jai, with whom he has a solid friendship. Together with the young people, Jai and Yama have built a community where “the only obligation is that you give back what you've learned.” The young rappers who come in are supported by older members who were there before them, and they in turn support those who arrive after.
<strong>Une initiative plus que nécessai: An initiative that is more than necessary
Le studio NBS assume une fonction crucia: NBS studio plays a crucial role in Côte-des-Neiges. Young people who live in the neighbourhood need to express themselves in order to thrive and, in their words, NBS is one of the few places where they can do that. With demand far exceeding what the studio can offer, NBS is “a victim of its success.” Getting an appointment for two hours of recording is becoming difficult. The wait for a studio session is now a month. Jai and the young people tell us the studio lacks funding, equipment and space. What's more, the program can only help young people aged 11 to 18.
Pour Jai, cela est très malheureux, car: For Jai, this is very unfortunate, because that is precisely the point in their lives when these young people need guidance the most. “Life gets very hard for young people when they finish high school, and unfortunately that's when we have to part ways with them,” the coordinator laments. In his view, more funding would allow the current project to continue and to improve.
Malgré tout, les jeunes entrevoient leur: Despite everything, the young people look to their future with optimism. When asked what they will do if their careers don't take off, they quickly dismiss the possibility. Many say they are about to break through with their music. They won't budge. Most say they immigrated with their parents. They came here to live under better skies, with better opportunities. They want to succeed at all costs. NBS studio has changed the way they see things. Individual success is no longer these young people's only goal, as young rapper KJ tells us. “I'm going to make it and bring all my brothers with me, because that's my family,” he says, speaking of the other young people who come to the studio.
Au studio NBS, un jeune est un projet de: At NBS studio, a young person is a project for society, for the community.
